Fetched via the Wayback Machine's capture of the live dps.sd.gov file (2025-03-17, HTTP 200, identical content digest to captures from 2024-06-06 and 2024-11-25, confirming the content was stable/unrevised across that period), because dps.sd.gov now permanently redirects every path -- including this exact file path -- to a new ServiceNow-based portal at www.sd.gov/dps that could not be scraped directly: plain HTTP fetch returns only an empty JS-app shell, and browser automation could not reach a stable/idle render state across repeated attempts. An extensive Wayback CDX search of the dps.sd.gov domain found no newer edition of this manual. Full text compiled to C:\claudews\passexamhq\temp\handbooks\sd\driver.txt. Exam mechanics (item count NOT publicly published anywhere found; passing score and retake policy ARE confirmed): passing score is 80% or higher on both the knowledge test and the driving test, per South Dakota DPS's own 'Driving Tests' and 'FAQs' pages (dps.sd.gov/driver-licensing/south-dakota-licensing-information/driving-tests and .../faqs), captured live via Wayback on 2025-06-05 and 2025-05-31 respectively (both HTTP 200, shortly before the same ServiceNow migration made them unreachable directly). Those same pages confirm up to 3 combined retake attempts within a 6-month testing-fee window (SDCL 32-12-2), and a mandatory 2-week wait if caught cheating. No official source found states the knowledge test is timed, nor states its total item count -- despite a thorough search (DPS site, archived FAQ/driving-tests pages, the manual itself), so those two facts are left unconfirmed rather than guessed, per project policy. Content-depth rationale: the manual is genuinely comprehensive (about 66 printed pages covering licensing/GDL, testing, points/suspension, insurance/registration, seatbelts/child restraints, alcohol & drug law, fitness to drive, signs/signals/markings, right-of-way/roundabouts, speed/space management, passing, parking, sharing the road with pedestrians/bicyclists/motorcycles/trucks/buses, emergency vehicles/traffic stops, school buses/work zones, crash/emergency procedures, and night/winter/rural driving), and it supports 219 distinct, well-grounded, non-repetitive questions after good-faith effort covering essentially every quiz-worthy fact in the source text. This lands below the site's usual 250-300 target; per the 'better nothing than nonsense' principle, no filler, invented statistics, or restated questions were added to pad the count further -- 219 is the honest ceiling this specific handbook supports.
